live_handoff.headline: SESSION 134 — the KG-critical parser_segv_braced_list_call_arg FIXED (the handoff's item 0). ROOT: a braced-init-list call argument had NO PARSE — parseCallFunc/parseCallMethod handed the bare '{' to parseExpression (no brace-head reading), flattening elements into separate arguments ('Too many parameters' on a valid call) or returning a NULL that parseExpr_identifierArm:34342 dereferenced (madcide died in-process opening examples/embed_hello.cpp). FIX, each at its owning layer: (1) respell_braced_list_for_target = THE re-spell owner, extracted VERBATIM from TokenRETURN::parse (class target -> functional form T{...} via parse_functional_type_expression's TokenObjTemp arm; non-class aggregate -> compound literal (T){...}; TokenRETURN adopts it); the call readers adopt via respell_braced_list_call_argument (target = callee parameter at this position: idx = tc->argc() + hidden-__this via function_uses_hidden_this — FuncDef::parameters carries the hidden slots; reference-stripped via referent_if_reference; call_signature_funcdef = the bound overload, so an overload-set mismatch errors loudly = slice limitation). (2) TokenObjTemp.braced (both build sites already knew open_id) + ctor_args_are_braced ObjTemp arm -> the EXISTING [dcl.init.list]/4 (il-ctor) and /5 (IS initializer_list — built from the array directly) arms in class_ctor_call serve functional-form temporaries. (3) initializer_list_literal emits the backing array SIZED ((E[N]){...}) — fixes the LATENT decl-path silent-wrong (std::initializer_list<E> l = {...} read GARBAGE elements in a later statement; testinitlist only read size()). (4) BELTS, loud never silent: parseExpression REFUSES a '{' HEAD ('braced-init-list is not supported in this context'); the call readers Throw on a NULL argument parse; parse_objtemp_ctor_arguments refuses nested-list elements. WARNING the bisect framing 'class temporaries / mid-position' was WRONG: plain longs + list-followed-by-any-argument crashed too, and the v1 flatten arity error was the SAME missing parse. DEEPER FIND 1 (silent wrong answer, jumped the queue): c2mir's N_COMPOUND_LITERAL check guard treated the N_ASSIGN NULL context barrier like a found owning N_SPEC_DECL, so nested compound literals in ASSIGNMENT context skipped check_initializer — an UNSIZED nested array literal's type was never completed (gen got size 8 at frame offset 0: il = (struct IL){(long long*)(long long[]){10,32}, 2} read garbage past [0] THROUGH THE WHOLE MADC PIPELINE from plain C; the uncast form SEGV'd gen; a sized type survived only because gen-time collect_init_els walks values anyway; a cast above the barrier accidentally ran the check — why standalone worked). Fix: a barrier stop = 'no owning declaration -> check HERE'; declaration-owned skips unchanged. STOCK-UPSTREAM defect -> third upstream-PR candidate (owner gates). The uncast nested form through raw c2m now gets the KNOWN loud 'excess elements in scalar initializer' (the spell-the-decay strictness cir_builder already documents; madc's front end wraps the cast itself, so madc is CORRECT). c2mir interp battery + bootstrap test green. DEEPER FIND 2: install-libmadc never shipped madc_typeid.h though installed madc_api.h includes it (the madc_pch.h hole's exact twin, one line below in the recipe) — every fresh-install downstream parse died at the first include; found mirroring the owner's /usr/local/include on the container (sudo make -C src install-libmadc now reproduces the owner environment there). PAYOFF: examples/embed_hello.cpp parses CLEAN through madc::parse_open — 0 problems, 123 spans, 18 comments (madcide safe + fully highlighted). TESTS: tests/testinitlistarg.mad (six shapes: crash/free-fn/explicit-functional/flatten/decl-later-read/single-element; g++ AND clang++ oracle exact) + tests/testnestedcomplit.mad (--std=c17; gcc AND clang oracle). emit-c++ echo verified: no synthetic-token leak (directive hoisting = the pre-existing shape; echo compiles clean under both oracles). DUPAUDIT (scoped, the brace seam): family braced_list_to_parseexpression consolidated+belted (the parseExpression head-brace Throw IS the gate — a grep gate is infeasible without false positives); braced-ness flags (Decl/ObjTemp/CtorInitializer) share ONE reader = ctor_args_are_braced, not divergent. RESIDUES (all LOUD, KG-banked): braced_list_decl_ctor_argument (P p("x", {V(1)}, &s) gets the belt error — the re-spell there needs a parse-time candidate-ctor rule; ctor overloads select at CIR); embed_hello_full_compile_residues (parse handle clean but FULL compile errors: installed-header lane = tsubst bail on std::vector<madc::value> range-ctor; -Iinclude lane = native_type is-not-a-class-type in program.h:192 — self-hosting arc, not madcide blockers).
settled: respell_braced_list_for_target = THE brace-list re-spell owner; a bare '{' must never HEAD parseExpression (the head-brace Throw = the runtime gate)
TokenObjTemp.braced is the functional-form twin of TokenDecl::ctor_args_braced; ctor_args_are_braced is the ONE reader

known_pre_existing_gaps: SCRIPT `value` IS NOT YET THE 32-BYTE madc_value STRUCT (recorded 2026-08-17, owner: not to be taken on now). Symptom: `value f()` returned BY VALUE emits `int f()` and silently returns nothing (exit 0, empty output) — func_def's return-type arm -> type_list -> append_type_specs has no dtARRAY case and falls through to int. That is why php::print_r returns madc::value & rather than madc::value. CORRECTED PREMISE: a C type DOES exist — madc_value (include/madc_api.h:52) is a tagged 32-byte aligned(16) struct, and madc::value merely CONTAINS it plus two unique_ptr members (32+8+8 = 48 = the emitted long long[6]); the opaque-buffer lowering exists because of those OWNING C++ members, not a missing type. MEASURED: _array/_object are private with no friends and all 40 refs are in ONE file (src/madc_value.cpp) — 12 mutations, 28 reads; the cell finalizer is already wired and called from generated code (cir_builder.cpp:25789/25797); the is_array_object sites would mostly RETIRE. HARD PART: the class deep-copies the containers while the cell path shares, so the migration needs copy-on-write at those 12 sites — a semantic change with its own oracled tests. Full write-up: docs/plans/2026-06-12-type-table-value-abi-design.md section 9. Sibling defect, also open: assigning to a `value &` PARAMETER is wrongly rejected ('assignment of incompatible value').

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.

MadArray/MadValue namespacing is an open API/ABI follow-up: moving the real C++ types to madc::array and madc::value would give PHP array helpers a normal namespace type surface, but compatibility aliases alone will not preserve old C++ mangled names.

Embedded <iostream> output remains partially staged: cout/cerr/clog still use header-defined stdio-backed ostream bodies. Follow-up is to replace that output surface with real libstdc++ declarations/operators, matching the std::cin direction; do not add stdio.h/FILE* stream bridges.
